paths.description: Entry URL and final geolocated regional notice; represents the public landing and unavailable primary downloader journey. No additional page archetypes are linked from this notice.

Unknown-URL 404 template; represents HTTP failure messaging and recovery navigation. The primary downloader, account, checkout, and form flows were not reachable because service is discontinued in the audit region.

findings.summary: The page ignores the user’s dark colour-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light capture; the computed body remains rgb(249, 249, 249), html color-scheme is normal, and the CSS contains no dark preference adaptation.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and add a prefers-color-scheme: dark palette with tested surface and text colours.

findings.summary: The regional service-discontinuation page is a dead end.
findings.evidence: The first viewport contains only a discontinuation letter. The rendered DOM has zero anchors or controls, so users cannot reach help, another region, or an explanation of available alternatives.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise next-steps section with real links to support, regional availability, policy details, and any lawful alternatives.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on the 404 recovery links.
findings.evidence: The focused-link probe successfully focuses the logo, homepage, contact, helper, and language controls, but every computed outlineStyle is none; some text links are only 16px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a strong :focus-visible outline with offset and ensure compact links have a minimum 44px touch target without inflating inline text links unnecessarily.

findings.summary: The notice explains the shutdown but provides no primary next action.
findings.evidence: The screenshot clearly states that UK service is discontinued, but the page has no button or link. Its document title and description still advertise a working YouTube downloader, contradicting the visible purpose.
findings.suggestedFix: Align title/description with the notice and add one clear, honest next action such as support or availability information.

findings.summary: The advertised video-download task cannot be started from the audited region.
findings.evidence: https://en1.savefrom.net redirects twice to https://gb.savefrom.net/ and renders a United Kingdom service-discontinuation notice. There is no form, input, button, or alternative task path.
findings.suggestedFix: If service is intentionally unavailable, stop advertising the downloader in metadata and provide a region-appropriate, lawful alternative or support path. If the redirect is erroneous, correct the geolocation/routing decision.

findings.summary: The service-unavailable state offers no recovery or continuation.
findings.evidence: The notice explains why service ended but exposes no retry, support, contact, region selector, or back/continue control. By contrast, the tested 404 template does provide Homepage and Contact us recovery links.
findings.suggestedFix: Reuse the 404 page’s recovery pattern on the discontinuation page and add relevant support and availability links.

findings.summary: A tiny notice incurs redirects and render-blocking CSS/font requests.
findings.evidence: The HAR records two 302 redirects before content, plus parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority style.css and Google Fonts stylesheets. Lighthouse LCP was 2.8s despite only 58KB transferred.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve the final notice directly, inline its small critical styles, remove unused font families, and avoid the redirect chain.

findings.summary: Nearly the entire shared stylesheet is unused on the notice.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 41,615 wasted bytes and 98.30% unused CSS in style.css; that file is also the largest network resource at 42,530 transferred bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Ship a dedicated minimal notice stylesheet or split shared CSS so this route downloads only the rules it uses.

findings.summary: The footer logo image has no accessible alternative.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails image-alt for img/logo_small2.svg; the image primitive confirms the image has no alt attribute.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the linked brand logo an appropriate alt value such as “Savefrom.net”, or alt="" only if the adjacent accessible text fully duplicates it.

findings.summary: The notice lacks semantic page structure, and recovery links suppress focus.
findings.evidence: The notice has no h1 and no main landmark; only header and footer are present. On the 404 archetype, focused anchors all compute outline-style:none.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark the notice heading as h1, wrap primary content in main, and add an obvious :focus-visible treatment throughout shared navigation.

findings.summary: The main notice restricts browser zoom.
findings.evidence: The rendered viewport meta is width=device-width, initial-scale=1, maximum-scale=1. Mobile layout itself has no horizontal overflow, but maximum-scale limits user magnification.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale=1 and retain a standard width=device-width, initial-scale=1 viewport declaration.

findings.summary: Search metadata describes a downloader that the page no longer provides.
findings.evidence: The visible page is “Discontinuation of Service in the United Kingdom”, while title is “YouTube Downloader - Download Youtube videos for free!” and meta description advertises video conversion.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a unique title and description that accurately identify the regional service notice.

findings.summary: The public notice is explicitly excluded from indexing and contains no crawlable navigation.
findings.evidence: Meta robots is noindex, nofollow and Lighthouse is-crawlable fails. The rendered notice has zero anchors, while /robots.txt returns a generic 404.
findings.suggestedFix: If the notice should answer users arriving from search, allow indexing/following and include real support links. Otherwise redirect retired indexed URLs to a canonical, indexable status page.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are absent or contradictory.
findings.evidence: The page has no canonical or hreflang, declares noindex/nofollow, and both robots.txt and sitemap.xml return 404. The 404 template itself declares index,follow, which risks indexing error URLs.
findings.suggestedFix: Define an intentional canonical/indexing policy, return valid robots.txt and sitemap responses, add hreflang for localized notices, and mark real 404 pages noindex.

findings.summary: HTTPS is used, but baseline security headers and cookie attributes are missing.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive finds no CSP, HSTS, or X-Content-Type-Options. Both country and lang cookies lack Secure and use SameSite=None; lang persists for 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, a restrictive CSP, nosniff, and set first-party preference cookies Secure with Lax/Strict SameSite and proportionate expiry.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are not configured.
findings.evidence: The response has no clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy, and no CSP frame-ancestors fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP frame-ancestors (or X-Frame-Options where needed), strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The localized experience does not use direction-ready layout primitives.
findings.evidence: The page language is correctly en, but html has no dir and CSS inspection found no logical property signals. The 404 exposes 20 localized links, so bidirectional/localized layout is an active concern.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an explicit direction where localization requires it and replace physical spacing/positioning with logical properties so RTL variants do not need fragile overrides.

findings.summary: Shared styling and font CSS are disproportionate to the static notice.
findings.evidence: Of 58,180 transferred bytes, style.css accounts for 42,530 bytes and Lighthouse says 98.30% is unused; an additional Google Fonts stylesheet blocks rendering.
findings.suggestedFix: Use system fonts or only the required font face and ship route-specific CSS for the notice.

taskList.title: Replace the dead-end regional landing with accurate metadata and a clear support/availability path
Add semantic structure, alt text, visible focus, and unrestricted zoom
Deploy baseline response security headers and secure cookie attributes
Remove redirect, unused shared CSS, and unnecessary font blocking
Make robots, canonical, sitemap, hreflang, and 404 indexing policy consistent
Use direction-ready logical CSS for localized variants
